title: Shiratama Dango (Rice Dumplings/Mochi Balls)
description: Shiratama Dango is a small chewy mochi ball typically served with Japanese desserts. You can enjoy them with fruits, ice cream or simply drizzled with syrup!

ingredients.name: glutinous rice flour (shiratamako (see separate measurements if using mochiko))

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Measure 100 g glutinous rice flour (shiratamako) into a bowl and give it a quick whisk. Measure 90 ml water into a jug and pour half of it into the bowl. (If using mochiko, add 90 g glutinous rice flour (mochiko) and 10 g potato starch (katakuriko) to a bowl and whisk. Measure 80 ml water and pour half into the bowl.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Mix with a spatula and add the rest of the water little by little until a dough forms (you might not need all of the water). Knead between each water addition until you have a smooth dough with the texture of an earlobe. Note: You do not need to use all of the water.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Start boiling a pot of water. While you wait, cut the dough in half and roll it into cylinders (if doubling or tripling the recipe, cut into quarters or sixths respectively). Cut each cylinder into 10 equal pieces then roll them into balls and press the center to make a dent.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Place on a piece of baking parchment to prevent sticking.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Once your water is boiling, gently place the shiratama dango into the pot and nudge them with chopsticks to stop them from sticking to the bottom of the pot. Boil until they float (approx 3 minutes).

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: When they are all floating, set a timer for 1 minute and prepare a bowl of ice cold water.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Turn off the heat and use a mesh spoon to transfer the cooked shiratama dango to the bowl of ice water. Leave to cool for 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Drain and serve topped with dark brown sugar syrup (kuromitsu) and roasted soybean powder (kinako) to taste. Enjoy!

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: If you have leftovers, place them spaced out on a tray lined with baking paper and freeze for 1 hour. After 1 hour, transfer to a sealable freezer bag and eat within 1 month. Thaw in the microwave (40-50 seconds 600W) or slowly in a bowl of water.

steps.title: Step 5

steps.title: Step 6

steps.title: Step 7

title: Homemade Kuromitsu (Japanese Brown Sugar Syrup)
description: Kuromitsu is a rich, sweet, and mildly bitter dark brown sugar syrup often served with traditional Japanese sweets. It's also great for drinks or ice cream!

ingredients.name: dark brown sugar (muscovado or kokuto if available)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Add 50 g dark brown sugar, 50 g white sugar and 120 ml water to a cold saucepan. Mix well and break any large lumps of sugar.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Transfer the pan to the stove and heat on medium. Stir continuously, and then it starts to bubble, reduce the heat to low. Continue to heat while stirring until all of the sugar has dissolved. If foam forms around the edges, scoop it out with a spoon.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Once the sugar has completely dissolved, continue to simmer until slightly thickened. It should be a similar thickness to simple syrup and will thicken further once cooled.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Remove from the heat and allow to cool before using. To store, transfer the cooled syrup to a clean glass container with an airtight lid and keep it in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks. Enjoy!

title: Egg Noodles for Ramen (Chijire Tamago Men)
description: Upgrade your homemade miso ramen with these chewy and irresistible hand crafted egg noodles!

ingredients.name: egg + water (whole egg plus filtered water, total 35% of flour weight. E.g. 50g egg + 55g water = 105g total liquid weight.)
salt (fine sea or kosher, avoid iodized)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Sift 300 g bread flour into a large bowl and make a well in the center.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Place a measuring jug on digital scales and set the weight to zero. Crack an egg into the jug to weigh it, and then top up with filtered water so that the total is 105 g egg + water. (See note if doubling or tripling the recipe.)

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add ½ tsp salt and whisk until the salt is completely dissolved and everything is combined.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Pour the mixture into the well in the flour little by little while whisking with chopsticks.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Whisk until large shaggy crumbs form.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Transfer to a sealable ziplock bag and rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: After 30 minutes, place the bag on the floor and knead it with your feet until it has pressed together to form a dough.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Remove the dough from the bag and fold it in half. Return it to the bag and knead with your feet again. Continue to fold and knead until the dough becomes smooth.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Return the dough to the bag, seal securely and refrigerate overnight, preferably 24 hours if time permits.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Transfer the dough to a clean surface and dust the top with potato starch (katakuriko). Roll it as thin as you can by hand and then cut it into 4 smaller pieces so that they fit the width of your pasta machine.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Starting with the widest setting (for me, it's "0"), roll each piece through the pasta machine. Reduce the thickness and repeat until your dough is about 1.5mm thick. (For me, I roll until I reach setting "5").

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Attach a 2-3mm cutting attachment and feed each piece through.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Sprinkle each batch with potato starch (katakuriko) to prevent sticking.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Gently knead and scrunch the noodles to create the wave effect. If you notice the noodles sticking together, add more starch.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil and boil the noodles for 1 minute 30 seconds. Alternatively, wrap and refrigerate for 2-3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Mentaiko Mayo Onigiri

steps.title: Step 2

steps.title: Step 3

steps.title: Step 4

steps.title: Step 5

steps.title: Step 6

description: These teriyaki meatballs are an easy and delicious Japanese dish to make for dinner! They’re plump and juicy and you could make them in advance for meal prep too.

ingredients.name: Ground Beef (Or any variety you prefer)
cm white part of scallions (Or 2 inch)

title: Ayu no Shioyaki (Salt Grilled Sweet Fish)
description: Ayu no Shioyaki is a popular Japanese street food consisting of salt grilled sweet fish served on a bamboo skewer. This simple cooking method creates a delicious crispy skin and allows the natural sweet flavor to shine through!

ingredients.name: whole ayu (sweetfish) (or other similar sized river fish)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Start by holding the sweetfish under running water while scraping off the natural protective layer from the skin with the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Press the area between the gills and tail to remove any digestive contents, then wash the surface once more and pat it dry with kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Start preheating your grill or broiler to medium-high (approx 190 °C (374 °F)).Take a bamboo skewer longer than the length of the fish. Hold the fish with the head pointing left, and push the skewer through the mouth and out the top around the gill area.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Gently curve the fish by bending the body towards you, and push the skewer through the middle and out the back.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Finally, bend the tail away from you and push the skewer through the end of the fish, a couple of centimeters (1 inch) before the tail.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Coat the fins and tail generously with salt.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Holding the skewer in one hand, sprinkle salt over the fish from a height of about 30cm (12") while turning until evenly seasoned all over. Wrap the end of the skewer with foil and then place the fish on a wire rack.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Once preheated, reduce the grill's heat to medium and place the fish under the heat source for 4-5 minutes or until the skin is nicely browned. If using a single-sided grill, flip and repeat on the other side. If using a double sided grill, reduce the heat to medium-low after 5 minutes and cook for a few extra minutes.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Serve immediately and drizzle with a squeeze of sudachi or lemon. Enjoy!

title: Grilled Mackerel Recipe (Saba Shioyaki)
description: Grilled salted mackerel, a delicious and easy fish entree for Japanese meal

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cover a frying pan with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Grate Daikon radish, and set aside.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Clean and fillet the fish or have your fish shop do it for you. Cut each fillet of mackerel in half. Sprinkle salt liberally on both sides of the fish.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Heat the frying pan at medium heat, and oil the surface of the aluminum foil lightly. Place the fish skin side down on the pan. Cook 4-5 minutes on each side, or until brown and cooked through.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Plate the fish, then add grated radish on the side, and pour some soy sauce on the radish if you want.

title: Tamagoyaki 卵焼き
description: How to make popular Tokyo street food "Kushidama" aka fluffy and bouncy Tamagoyaki

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Crack the eggs into a medium size mixing bowl.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Add seasoning (add shirodashi and water for dashimaki or add sugar, salt and water for atsumaki) and mix them all together gently to avoid too much bubble forming.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Strain the egg mixture through a sieve a few times.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Pour about 2tbsp oil (*not listed in the ingredients) in a small bowl and soak kitchen paper and set aside.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat till you can feel the heat when you hover your hand over the pan.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Pour 1/3 of egg mixture into the pan (you should hear a sizzling sound).

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Break any bubbles that have formed with the edge of the chopsticks and scramble gently and slightly .

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: When the surface is solidified a little, fold and push the egg to one end of the pan with chopsticks *2

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Wipe the empty side of the pan with oil-soaked kitchen paper and pour another 1/3 of the egg mixture into the empty space of the pan.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Lift the folded egg up to let the egg mixture run under it.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Fold and roll the egg from one side of the pan and wipe the empty space of the pan with the oil-soaked kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Pour the last 1/3 of egg mixture and repeat fold and roll.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Turn the heat off and wrap the rolled egg with thin kitchen towel.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Roll the wrapped egg roll with a sushi mat to shape and rest to cool down.*3

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Once it is cool down slice it 2cm (7.9inch) thick and serve.

title: Asparagus Tempura
description: With its delicate flavor and crunchy texture, this asparagus tempura is perfect for dipping and makes a delicious appetizer or snack!

ingredients.name: cooking oil (neutral flavor for deep frying)
unbleached cake flour (or starch for dusting)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Before you start, chill all of the tempura ingredients thoroughly. Sift 15 g cornstarch and 75 g unbleached cake flour into a bowl and place it in the freezer. Keep 75 ml cold water, 50 ml carbonated water (sealed) and 1 egg yolk in the fridge until right before mixing. (At least 30 minutes)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Start heating your cooking oil to 170 °C (338 °F). While you wait, wash 8 stalks asparagus and pat them dry with kitchen paper. Break off the woody stems, taking about 1cm/ ½ inch off the bottom of the stalks. If you have a small cooking pot, cut each stalk in half.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: When your oil is almost ready, take a mixing bowl and add the 75 ml cold water, 50 ml carbonated water and 1 egg yolk straight from the fridge. Whisk gently until combined.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Take the dry ingredients from the freezer and add them to the egg mixture in 3 additions. Instead of whisking, use chopsticks to draw crosses in the batter until there is no more dry flour. Be careful not to overmix, lumps are fine in tempura batter.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: If you are making multiple batches or are in a warm environment, add a few ice cubes to the batter.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Coat the asparagus in a thin layer of unbleached cake flour. Tap off any excess, too much flour can cause the batter to fall off.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Once the oil is hot, dip the asparagus into the batter and place straight into the pot. Deep fry for 90 seconds or until the bubbles have settled down and the batter is lightly golden.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Transfer to a wire rack to drain excess oil.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Serve with salt, your favorite dipping sauce, or as part of a larger assortment of tempura. Enjoy!

title: Anago no Tempura (Conger Eel Tempura)
description: Conger eel makes the most delicious tempura and in this recipe, I'll teach you everything you need to know to make it perfectly every time!

ingredients.name: conger eel fillets (whitespotted, butterflied fillets (see note))
cooking oil (neutral flavor for deep frying)
unbleached cake flour (or starch for dusting)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Before starting this recipe, be sure to chill all of the tempura ingredients thoroughly (including the dry ingredients - I put them in the freezer).While you wait, place 4 conger eel fillets in a bowl and sprinkle with 2 tbsp salt. Massage the salt over the fillets to help break down the slimy layer on the surface, then wash thoroughly with running water.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Lay the conger eel fillets flat on a cutting board with the skin side facing up. Cover it with kitchen paper, then pour hot water (around 70 °C (158 °F)) over the top to reveal the slime which will turn white.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Use the blunt side of a knife to gently scrape off the slime, then dry them thoroughly with kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: If your fillets are particularly thick, make small vertical cuts along the flesh side about 3-4mm apart and a little over halfway through the flesh. This will break any remaining small bones.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Cut the fillets into 15cm/6" pieces, or your preferred size that fits inside your cooking pot.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Start heating your cooking oil to 180 °C (356 °F) - 190 °C (374 °F). Dust the surface of the eel fillets with a thin layer unbleached cake flour and brush off any excess.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: When your oil is almost ready, take a mixing bowl and add 75 ml cold water, 50 ml carbonated water and 1 egg yolk straight from the fridge. Whisk gently until combined.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Mix 15 g cornstarch and 75 g unbleached cake flour together in a small bowl, then add it to the egg mixture in 3 batches. Rather than whisking, use chopsticks to draw crosses in the mixture until there is no more dry flour. Lumps are perfectly okay, do not overmix.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: If you are making multiple batches or are in a warm environment, add a few ice cubes to the batter.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Once the oil is hot, dip the flour-dusted eel fillets in the batter and then place them straight into the pot. Fry in batches to avoid overcrowding the pot.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: After 1 minute, sprinkle a small amount of extra batter over the fillets for added texture.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Fry for about 3-5 minutes or until the batter becomes lightly browned, then transfer to a wire rack to drain the excess oil.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Serve immediately with tempura dipping sauce (tentsuyu), a sprinkle of salt, and some grated daikon radish (daikon oroshi). Enjoy!

title: Omurice オムライス
description: Omurice, Omelette Rice, is a popular and tasty Japanese dish made from ketchup flavoured chicken fried rice wrapped in an egg omelette.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Chop the chicken, onion, carrot, and capsicum into small cubes.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add the chicken to the pan and cook until the meat has all turned white.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Add the vegetables and cook until the onion becomes translucent.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Add the ketchup and mix it all together.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Add the rice and mix in until the rice is all coated with the ketchup.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Add thawed frozen pea to the ketchup rice and mix them together.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Flavour with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Remove from heat and set aside in a large bowl.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: In a small bowl crack and beat 2 eggs.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Heat the large frying pan with 1/2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat and pour in the egg, allowing it to spread all over the bottom frying pan and slightly scramble the middle without breaking the omelette.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Turn off the heat, and pour half the ketchup rice into the centre of the omelette.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Push the omelette and rice to one side of the pan and fold in the sides of the omelette to wrap the rice.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Hold a plate beside the omelette and tip the pan a bit to slide the omelette on to the plate so that it flips on to the plate so the egg is on top covering the rice.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Repeat these steps again for the next 2 eggs and remaining chicken rice then serve!

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Serve on a plate and sprinkle on sesame seeds.

title: Eggplant and Ground Beef Curry
description: Curry with eggplant and ground beef over steamed rice

ingredients.name: large egg plant (or 4 Japanese eggplants, 1" cubed)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Heat oil, ginger, and garlic in a large pot. Add meat and cook until browned, then add onion (and carrot if using) and cook until soft. Finally add cubed eggplant and stir.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Add water to the pot. After it boils, skim any fat, and reduce heat to medium low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Remove from heat and add curry sauce mix. Stir well so the pieces of the mix dissolve.

steps.title: Step 4

steps.title: Step 5

title: Negitoro Onigiri (Minced Tuna Rice Ball)
description: Negitoro Onigiri is a delicious rice ball filled with perfectly soft minced sashimi-grade tuna and fresh green onions. This recipe beats convenience store versions hands down!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Shiojime (optional step for improved texture & flavor). Wash and dry 60 g sashimi grade tuna block, then sprinkle with salt all over and place it in a container. Store the container in the fridge for 10-15 minutes with one side elevated to drain the excess moisture. Wash off the salt and pat dry with kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Use a spoon to scrape the tuna flesh.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Chop with a knife until it becomes roughly mashed.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Place the mashed tuna in a bowl and add ½ tbsp Japanese mayonnaise, ½ tsp cooking oil and ⅛ tsp dashi granules. Mix until combined.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Measure out 440 g cooked Japanese short-grain rice and divide it into equal portions. If using a rice ball mold, sprinkle a pinch of salt into the mold and add half a portion (approx 55g / 2oz) of rice. Make a dent in the center and add a spoonful of mashed tuna.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: If shaping by hand, wet your hands and sprinkle them with a pinch of salt. Take a portion of rice (approx 110g / 4oz) and spread it flat on your palm, placing the tuna in the center. (Wet hands to prevent sticking.)

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Top the tuna with a small blob of wasabi and a few finely chopped green onions. Add 1 drop of Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu).

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: For the mold, cover with the other half of the rice and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. For hand-shaping, fold the rice over and then shape into a rounded triangle.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Wrap with nori and enjoy!

title: Homemade Udon Noodle Recipe
description: Homemade fresh Udon noodles good in hot or cold Udon dishes

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Mix warm water and salt well until the salt is dissolved.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: In the bowl of a stand mixer, add salt water and flour. Mix with a dough hook at medium speed about 5 minutes. Wrap the dough in plastic and let it rest at least 3 hours in the refrigerator (preferably overnight).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Take the cold dough from the refrigerator and let it return to room temperature. ((Remove from plastic and knead by hand for a couple of minutes until the dough becomes smooth and elastic. Cover and let it rest for 20 minutes.)) Put the dough in a strong 1 gallon plastic bag (such as a zip freezer bag), leaving it at least partly open to allow air to escape. Then put the bag of dough on the floor. Step on the bag of dough and knead with your feet until the dough spreads out, taking up the whole bag. Take the dough out and fold in half twice, into a smaller square. Repeat this kneading and folding 2 more times. Shape the dough into a ball and let it rest 20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Roll out the dough to 3 mm (1/8") thick about the size of 50cm x 35cm (20" x14") sheet, dusting well with a lot of flour so that it doesn't stick, and fold the dough into 3 layers. Cut the dough to 3 mm width noodles.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Boil water in a big pot, and boil the noodles for 10-15 minutes. Strain and wash. Use as directed in recipes.

title: Aunt Keiko's Inarisushi いなり寿司
description: Special Inari sushi recipe from my aunt with step by step photos & video. including a secret ingredient to enhance the fragrance and enrich the flavour.

ingredients.name: abura age (cut them in half and make 12)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cook and prepare the sushi rice (my sushi rice uses 2 cups of uncooked rice and I used about 2/3 of the entire cooked rice) *1

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Cut the aburaage pieces in half.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Pour boiling hot water over the aburaage to remove the excess oil.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Bring one cup of water in a saucepan to boil over high heat and add dashi powder.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Add sugar, soy sauce to the saucepan.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Turn the heat down to medium, add aburaage and cook for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Add miso paste and cook until all liquid has absorbed and evaporated.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Turn the heat off and cool it down completely.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Make 12 round and cylinder shape sushi rice balls (each weigh about 50 g)

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Open the aburaage pouch gently without breaking and insert one sushi rice ball and close the end side down.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Repeat this same process for the rest of the 11 aburaage and rice balls.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Serve on a plate and sprinkle black sesame seeds on top.

title: Negitoro Maki (Mashed Tuna Sushi Rolls)
description: Negitoro is a golden combination of melt-in-mouth mashed tuna and refreshing green onions. With my recipe and secret tips, you can make restaurant-worthy negitoro sushi rolls at home!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Optional "shiojime" to improve flavor: Rinse 120 g sashimi grade tuna block with cold water and pat it dry with kitchen paper. Sprinkle with salt all over, then place it in a container propped up on one side to allow excess moisture to drip to the bottom. Rest in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes, in the meantime you can prepare the rice.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Mix 2 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar (komezu), 1 tsp sugar and ½ tsp salt in a bowl until dissolved.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Pour the mixture over warm 280 g cooked Japanese short-grain rice, and mix using a cut and fold motion with the edge of a rice paddle while fanning to cool. Once evenly distributed, cover the rice with a clean damp tea towel to prevent it drying out and set aside.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Wash the tuna and pat it dry with kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Use a spoon to scrape the tuna flesh into rough pieces.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Roughly chop it with a knife to make a chunky mash.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Transfer the mashed tuna to a bowl and add 1 tbsp Japanese mayonnaise, ½ tbsp cooking oil and ¼ tsp dashi granules. Mix until everything is combined.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Optional: Turn your gas burner on low and carefully fan 2 sheets roasted seaweed for sushi (nori) over the fire to improve the texture and aroma of the nori.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Fold the nori in half and pinch along the crease before tearing them down the fold. (Use scissors for a neater cut.)

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Lay the bamboo rolling mat on a flat surface with the bamboo sticks laying horizontally. Place a piece of nori rough side facing up at the bottom of the mat.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Wet your hands and shape an 70g (approx 2.5 oz) handful of rice into a rough cylinder.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Place the rice on the nori and spread it out while leaving a finger-width border along the top. Pinch along the top edge of the rice to make a ridge, then spread wasabi through the middle.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Spread quarter of the tuna mixture through the middle of the rice, then sprinkle finely chopped green onions next to it.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Lift the bottom of the mat fold over until the rice meets.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Press firmly to shape, then lift the edge of the mat and roll once more so that the edge of the nori seals the roll.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.description: Wipe a sharp knife with a damp cloth and cut the sushi roll in half. Use a short, sharp sawing motion to cut the roll without applying too much pressure (pressing down will squash it).

steps.title: Step 17
steps.description: Cut each half into thirds, wiping the knife between each cut.

steps.title: Step 18
steps.description: Enjoy with a small bowl of Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) for dipping.

title: Stir Fry Vegetables

steps.title: Step 4

title: Garlic Miso Rice Balls

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice (approx 1/3 rice cooker cup per rice ball before cooking)

steps.title: Step 1

steps.title: Step 2

Alternatively, shape by hand making sure to wet your hands before handling the rice to prevent sticking and sprinkle your palms with salt to season the outside. title: Sata Andagi Okinawan doughnuts 沖縄ドーナツサタアンダギー
description: Crunchy outside, moist inside, these round Sata Andagi, also known as Okinawan doughnuts are delicious. Recipe with step by step photos, and a video to make them successfully at home.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Sift flour and baking powder together and set it aside.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Crack the eggs into a mixing bowl and whisk.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add the oil into the bowl and combine them all together.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Fold the flour into the egg mixture by cutting action with wooden spatula in order to avoiding overmix them.

steps.title: Step 5
