steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Take about 1 tbsp of dough for each doughnut. Shape the mixture into 8 balls the size of ping pong balls.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Heat oil over medium heat to 150°C ( 300°F) *5

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Deep fry the dough balls slowly. When the dough is cooked slowly, the outside becomes crispy first and then the inside cooks slowly. Because the air expands inside the ball, it creates a crack in the outside.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: When doughnuts balls crack and golden brown in colour, remove from the oil and drain the excess oil on cooling lack lined with kitchen paper.

title: Sushi Rolls (Tuna and Cucumber Rolls) Recipe
description: Skinny sushi rolls filled with tuna sashimi and cucumber

ingredients.name: Nori roasted seaweed (8" X 7 1/2" (21 cm x 19cm))

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cut Roasted Seaweed in half (4 x 7 1/2" or 10 x 19cm). Cut tuna into 1/2" (1cm) thick pieces and 7 1/2" (19cm) long. Cut cucumber into the same size, cutting out seeds. (It's OK not to have one 7 1/2" long piece, just add pieces together to make the total length.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Put a sushi mat flat on your work surface with the bamboo slats left to right, so you can roll the mat away from you. Place a piece of seaweed on the sushi mat with one of the seaweed's long sides close to the front edge of the sushi mat (the edge near you). Spread about 1/4 cup sushi rice on the seaweed leaving a 1" (2.5cm) space along the far edge of the seaweed. Place tuna or a cucumber strip on the middle of rice. Holding the filling down, roll from the front end of the mat guiding with the sushi mat toward the other end. Tighten the rolls like roll cakes, pulling the mat to tighten. Remove the roll from the mat.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Cut a roll into 8 pieces. Serve with soy sauce and Wasabi.

title: PIckled Daikon (My Aunt Keiko's Recipe) 大根の漬物
description: The best pickled Daikon Radish recipe from my aunt Keiko

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Wash the daikon radish and slice it about 15cm long and 5mm thickness.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Sprinkle salt over the sliced daikon and toss them to evenly coat daikon with salt.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Leave it for 6-7 hours.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Combine the rice vinegar, mirin, and sugar in a small saucepan. Bring it to boil over medium heat, when all the sugar has dissolved, turn the heat off and let it cool down.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: After 6-7 hours, drain and squeeze out the excess water off the sliced daikon radish. ( do not wash them )

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Lay the daikon radish into a large container and sprinkle a little bit of bonito flake, kelp, and vinegar mixture. Repeat the process until all the ingredients are used.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Leave it in room temperature for a week.

title: Eggplant Kabayaki (Plant-Based "Unagi" Bowl)
description: This melt-in-mouth Eggplant Kabayaki is mind-blowingly tender and coated in an unbeatably easy and delicious kabayaki-style sauce. It's budget-friendly, plant-based and only takes 20 minutes!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Peel 3 eggplants and place them in a heatproof bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and microwave for 3 minutes at 600W.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: While the eggplant cools, take a small bowl and mix 1 tbsp dark brown sugar, 2 tbsp Japanese dark soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu), 2 tbsp sake and 1 ½ tbsp mirin. Set by the stove for later.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Once cool enough to touch, cut the eggplants down the middle lengthways without cutting all the way through. Open it out like a book, making several more incisions to help open it further.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Press the surface with the surface of your knife to help flatten it further.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Start heating your pan over a medium heat. While you wait, sprinkle the cut side of the eggplants with ½ tbsp all-purpose flour.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Once hot, drizzle 1 tbsp cooking oil into the pan and place the eggplants inside with the flour-dusted side facing down.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Once golden, carefully flip the eggplants with a spatula and brown on the other side.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Pour in the sauce from earlier and carefully move the eggplants around the pan to fully coat them in the sauce. Continue to cook until the sauce has thickened, then remove the pan from the heat.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Divide 2 portions cooked Japanese short-grain rice between serving bowls and brush with the leftover sauce from the pan. Sprinkle with kizami nori (shredded nori). For a spicy kick, add some wasabi to the rice.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Place the eggplant kabayaki on top, then sprinkle with finely chopped green onions and toasted white sesame seeds. Enjoy!

title: Salmon Flakes Recipe
description: Salty salmon flakes, perfect topping for steamed rice and noodles

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Preheat oven to 425F (220C.) Place salmon on a greased baking sheet and cook in the oven for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Using fork, flake the salmon finely on the baking sheet. Remove any bones and skin.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Heat a non-stick frying pan on medium heat and add salmon flakes and Sake. Stirring constantly, cook until the fish is dry and moisture is evaporated. Add salt, Mirin, and sesame. Continue frying for a few more minutes. Remove from heat and cool completely.

title: Hiyashi Chuka with Goma(Sesame) dressing 冷やし中華
description: Hiyashi Chuka Cold Ramen is a refreshing Japanese cold noodle dish. All you need to know about how to make this dish with different topping and sauce options.

ingredients.name: packets of store bought ramen noodles

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Making sauce

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Hiyashi Chuka(cold noodle)

title: Natto Maki (Fermented Soybeans Sushi Rolls)
description: Savor the flavor of natto with this simple, delicious and budget-friendly sushi roll. Whether you're trying natto for the first time or a seasoned natto-lover, sushi rolls are a perfect way to enjoy this unique ingredient!

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice (approx 1 rice cup (raw) makes 4 rolls)
packs natto ("hikiwari" finely chopped type - approx 1/2 pack per roll)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Mix 1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar (komezu), 1 tsp sugar and ½ tsp salt together in a bowl until dissolved.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Pour the mixture over 320 g cooked Japanese short-grain rice while still warm. Mix gently yet thoroughly using a rice paddle while fanning to cool, then cover with a clean damp tea towel to prevent it from drying out.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Optional: Turn your gas burner on low and carefully fan 2 sheets roasted seaweed for sushi (nori) over the fire to improve the texture and aroma.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Fold the nori in half, pinch along the crease and then neatly tear down the fold. (Use scissors if preferred.)

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Place your bamboo rolling mat on a flat surface in front of you with the bamboo laying horizontally. With the rough side facing up, align the long side of the nori with the bottom of the mat.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Wet your hands and take a handful of sushi rice (approx 80g / ½ US cup). Shape it into a rough cylinder.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Spread the rice out to the edges leaving a border along the top, pinching along the top edge of the rice to make a ridge. Thoroughly mix 2 packs natto until foamy, then spread the natto through the middle, using half a packet per roll.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Lift the bottom of the mat and roll until the edges of the rice meet.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Press firmly, then lift the edge of the mat and roll once more to seal.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Wipe a sharp knife with a damp cloth and cut the sushi roll in half.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Cut each half into thirds, wiping the knife between each cut.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Enjoy with a small bowl of Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) for dipping!

title: Red Bean Paste 餡子
description: Red bean paste is a classic ingredient in many Japanese desserts and snacks. It is easy to make at home if you follow the tips with step by step photos.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Tsubu-an (mashed red bean paste)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Koshi-an (Smooth red bean paste)

title: Japanese Curry Powder from Scratch
description: This harmonious blend of 18 herbs and spices has been carefully crafted, allowing you to make your own authentic Japanese-style curry from scratch!

ingredients.name: cinnamon stick (approx 1 ½ inch long (or ½ tsp ground cinnamon))
dried red chili pepper ((or ½ tsp chili powder))
green cardamom pods ((or ¾ tsp cardamom powder))

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Place the whole spices (1 cinnamon stick, 1 star anise, 1 bay leaf, 1 dried red chili pepper, 4 green cardamom pods and 4 clove pods) in a spice blender and grind to a fine powder. (You can also use a mortar and pestle for this but it will take longer.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Once fine, pour the mixture into a dry frying pan.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add the rest of the spices.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Place the pan on the stove and heat over medium for 1-2 minutes. Stir continuously to prevent burning and encourage even cooking. Toast for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant and the color has turned to a rich brown.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Remove the pan from the stove and transfer your homemade Japanese curry powder to an airtight jar and store in a cool, dark place.

title: Matcha Green Tea Ice-cream 抹茶アイス
description: Flavour your next Ice-cream with matcha green tea. Matcha Green tea ice-cream seems the latest ice-cream flavour trend. It is easy and delicious to make.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Bring the milk and cream to a simmer over low heat in a sauce pan.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Turn the heat off and set aside.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Whisk 2 egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until the colour of the mixture becomes pale and fluffy.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Add the matcha green tea powder to the sugar and yolk mixture and mix well.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Gradually pour the warm milk mixture into the egg mixture and keep whisking until smooth.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Strain the mixture into a clean sauce pan and place over low heat for 5 minutes, continuously stirring.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Leave it in the fridge to chill.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Pour the matcha green tea mixture into an ice cream maker. *1

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Run the ice cream maker for about 20 minutes, and once the mixture has become thicker, pour it into a container and freeze it until set.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Serve with red bean paste, dango and strawberry(optional)

title: Ichiban Dashi
description: Combination base stock of bonito flakes and sea kelp for soup and other dishes

ingredients.name: sheet Kombu dried sea kelp ("4 x 2" (10 cm x 5 cm) )

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Put Kombu in water in a pot, and heat at medium heat until just before boiling. Remove Kombu.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Add Katsuobushi and let the water boil, then immediately turn off the heat. Leave it for 5 minutes and strain.

title: Spagghetti with Shimeji mushroom
description: Japanese flavored spaghetti with Shimeji mushrooms and smokey bacon

ingredients.name: Shimeji mushrooms (cut the bottom, separated into pieces by hand)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Boil about 12 cups or 3 littler of water in a big pot and add about 3 Tbsp salt (not in the ingredients). Cook spaghetti according to the instructions on the package.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Heat a frying pan at medium heat. Add bacon pieces and cook until browned and somewhat crispy. Add minced garlic and stir. Add Shimeji mushrooms and sliced onion and cook until tender. Add into the pan a quarter cup of boiling water from the pasta, the soy sauce, Mirin, and Sake, and stir well. Add butter in the sauce. Put the cooked spaghetti into the sauce, then add green onions. Stir for a couple of minutes to coat the spaghetti with the sauce.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Serve on a plate, and top with thinly cut Oba leaves and seaweed.

title: Homemade Ikura (Marinated Salmon Roe)
description: Ikura is a luxurious ingredient made with vibrant orange salmon roe soaked in a flavor-enhancing marinade and is used in sushi and rice bowls.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Open 1 sack salmon roe by hand (do not use a knife) and place it in a large heatproof bowl. Gently massage to help loosen the roe, and remove what you can from the membrane. (Don't worry about removing all of them at this point.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Pour 1000 ml water into a pot and add 1 tsp salt. Mix and heat until it reaches 70 °C (158 °F).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Pour the hot water over the salmon roe and separate the roe from the membrane using chopsticks, removing the membrane as you go.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Once you've removed all of the membrane and separated all of the roe, pour the contents of the bowl through a sieve to drain. Fill the bowl with cold water and gently wash the roe to remove any leftover debris. Drain and repeat until clean.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Drain once more and set the sieve of roe over an empty bowl. Sprinkle with ½ tsp salt and shake to evenly distribute it through the roe. Cover with plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator for 1 hour.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: While you wait, make the marinade. Add 60 ml sake and 30 ml mirin to a saucepan and boil for 30 seconds to release the alcohol.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Pour the sake and mirin mixture into a container and add 45 ml dashi stock, 30 ml Japanese light soy sauce (usukuchi shoyu) and 3 g dried kelp (kombu). Cool completely before adding the roe.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Transfer the roe to the marinade, make sure they are all submerged. Cover with a lid and marinate for 24 hours in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Enjoy with sushi or donburi!

title: Chikuzenni
description: Simmered Japanese vegetables like lotus root, carrot, and bamboo shoot along with chicken

ingredients.name: Takenoko (Bamboo Shoot, boiled, cut into pieces 1" thick 2" long)
chicken breast or 2 thighs (cut into 2" pieces)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Hydrate dried Shiitake mushrooms in water in a medium bowl.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Blanch the snow peas in boiling water or Dashi with a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Cut Konnyaku into 1/2" thick pieces, make 1/2" slit in the middle of the piece, and thread an end through the hole to make like a twisted rope (you can blanch them as well if you don't like the smell).

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Cut carrot into 1/2" thick rounds, then cut with a flower shaped cookie cutter (please watch the video to see how to cut for a 3-D effect).

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: In a large pot, add oil and heat at medium heat. When the oil becomes hot, add chicken pieces and cook until brown (no need to cook through). Add all vegetables except the Shiitake and the snow peas and cook and stir for a couple of minutes. Then add Shiitake and Dashi, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes until vegetables become soft.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Add sugar, soy sauce, Sake, and Mirin, stir, and cook another 15-20 minutes uncovered.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Remove from heat and let it continue to cook, covered, so the meat and vegetables absorb flavor from the soup. Serve with snow peas as garnish.

title: Yaki Udon 焼きうどん
description: Delicious and easy Yaki Udon recipe with step by step photos, and a video, including tips to make Japanese fried Udon noodle successfully.

ingredients.name: Bonito flakes and red pickled ginger for garnish

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Slice the pork fillet thinly and place in a mixing bowl.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Add sake, soy sauce and ginger into the mixing bowl to marinate the pork for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Cut all the vegetables into bite size pieces and set aside.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Mix all the sauce ingredients (soy sauce, sugar, oyster sauce, sake, mashed garlic, and grated ginger) in a small bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Cook the udon noodles in boiling water for a couple minutes and drain the cooking water well.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Heat sesame oil in a large frying pan over high heat and add finely chopped garlic and ginger till it aroma.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Add the pork fillet and cook till it's colour changed to grayish colour.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Add the vegetables and stir fry for a couple minutes.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Add the udon noodle and toss all together.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Pour over the sauce mixture and mix them together well.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Serve on a plate and top with bonito flakes and red pickled ginger.

title: Kushiage (Japanese Deep-Fried Skewers)
description: Kushiage is a fun and exciting dish made with a variety of meat, vegetables and seafood coated in a crunchy panko batter, deep fried and served with a tangy, addictive dipping sauce. It's easy to customize and great for parties!

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (or cake flour, plus extra for dusting if necessary)
dashi stock (use plant-based for vegetarians and vegans)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Start by cutting and drying all of your ingredients, then thread them onto bamboo skewers. For smaller ingrients like quail eggs or shrimp, you can stack 2-3 on one skewer (however, keep in mind the depth of your cooking oil).

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Take a small saucepan and add 80 ml Worcestershire sauce, 60 ml dashi stock, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp red wine and 1 tsp tomato ketchup. Mix well and boil for 1 minute over a medium heat, then set aside for later.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Start heating oil for deep frying to 170 °C (338 °F) to 180 °C (356 °F). While you wait, combine 150 g all-purpose flour, 250 ml cold water and 1 egg in a large mixing bowl until smooth. Prepare one more plate with 150 g panko breadcrumbs.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: When your oil is ready, dip the skewered ingredients into the batter one at a time before rolling in the panko breadcrumbs. (Tip: If your ingredients are slippery, it can be worthwhile to coat them in a light dusting of flour before battering.)

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Once fully coated in breadcrumbs, carefully place the skewers into the oil and fry for approximately 3 minutes or until golden. (This time is an estimate and depends on the thickness of your ingredients.)

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Fry in small batches to avoid lowering the oil temperature too much. I recommend frying each ingredient at the same time (e.g. meat together, vegetables together etc.)

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Remove the cooked skewers from the oil and transfer them to a wire rack to drain.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Serve with your homemade dipping sauce and enjoy!

title: Namasu Recipe
description: Daikon radish and carrot salad with sweet rice vinegar dressing

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Slice Daikon radish and carrot very thinly into 2" (5cm) lengths. Add salt and leave for 5 minutes. Squeeze out water from the cut radish and carrot. Cut the Kombu very thinly and add to the vegetables.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Put the rest of the ingredients in a pot, let it boil, and cool.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add vinegar mixture to the vegetables and mix. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

title: Authentic Kakiage (Mixed Vegetable Tempura)
description: Learn how to make authentic Japanese kakiage, a delicious dish made with a variety of thinly sliced vegetables encased in a light and crispy tempura batter. Serve on its own, or enjoy with udon or soba noodles!

ingredients.name: boiled shrimp (cut into 1 cm pieces (omit for vegetarians))
tsuyu sauce (noodle soup base) (diluted, optional for dipping)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Before you start, make sure the batter ingredients are thoroughly chilled. Mix 150 g unbleached cake flour and 30 g cornstarch in a bowl and place in the freezer for 30 minutes. You can use this time to cut the vegetables.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Dry the cut ½ yellow onions, ½ carrot, 6 boiled shrimp and 5 green beans with kitchen paper and place them in a bowl. Sprinkle with 1 tbsp unbleached cake flour and mix until evenly coated.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Preheat a small pan of cooking oil to 180 °C (356 °F). Use a small pan and fry one at a time to improve the shape. While you wait for the oil to heat up, crack 1 egg into a bowl and add 150 ml water and 100 ml carbonated water. Whisk gently until combined.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: If the egg mixture becomes foamy, scoop the bubbles out with a spoon.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Pour the chilled dry ingredients into a sieve. Sift into the egg mixture one-third at a time and draw crosses using chopsticks to help prevent over mixing. It's okay if the final result has a few lumps.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Add 3 ice cubes to the batter.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Pour the batter into the bowl with the vegetables and shrimp and mix until evenly coated.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Once the oil is hot, scoop up a ladleful of mixture and carefully slide it into the hot oil. Be careful not to scoop up too much batter, focus on lifting up the ingredients.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Fry for 1 minute and 30 seconds on each side.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Transfer to a wire rack to drain any excess oil. Continue to fry one kakiage at a time.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Serve with sea salt or diluted tsuyu sauce (noodle soup base) for dipping and enjoy!

title: Ochazuke Recipe
description: Steamed rice with salty salmon and other toppings, with green tea poured over

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Put rice crackers in a plastic bag and smash them to coarse pieces. Prepare hot green tea.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Put rice in a rice bowl, top with cracker pieces, salmon flakes, seaweed, sesame seeds, and wasabi. Pour hot green tea over rice. Add a little soy sauce if you want.

title: Japanese mochi ice cream 餅アイス
description: Japanese mochi ice cream recipe

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Scoop ice cream about 30g each with an ice cream/cookie dough scooper into an aluminium foil-layered small muffin tin and keep them in the freezer until its ready to wrap with mochi

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Making mochi sheets

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Wrapping ice cream with mochi sheets

title: Dashimaki Tamago Recipe
description: Fluffy and juicy Tamagoyaki rolled omelet with Dashi stock

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Heat a pan at medium high temperature and add oil. (A rectangular Tamagoyaki pan is best, but a round pan can work as well.)

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Pour a thin layer of egg mixture in the pan, tilting to cover the bottom of the pan. After the thin egg has set a little, gently roll into a log. Start to roll when the bottom of the egg has set and there is still liquid on top. If you let the egg cook too much, it will not stick as you roll the log. Now you have a log at one end of the pan. Pour some more egg mixture to again cover the bottom of the pan, with the roll of egg at the end. After the new layer has set, roll the log back onto the the cooked thin egg and roll to the other end of the pan. (You can also keep rolling in one direction by sliding the rolled egg back to the same end of the pan before adding more egg.)

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Repeat adding egg to the pan and rolling until the egg mixture is used up.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Remove the egg log from the pan onto a sushi mat, roll up lightly, and let it cool for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Unwrap the sushi mat and slice the log into 1/2" thick pieces. You should see a wavy pattern along the edge of the cross section of the egg from the mat.

title: Japanese Sake Steamed Clams (with Butter & Soy Sauce)
description: Asari no Sakamushi is a simple Japanese dish made with clams steamed with sake. Enjoy the rich flavors of butter and soy sauce combined with tender steamed clams, a perfect appetizer or side!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Start by placing 450 g clams in a colander and rinse with running water. Prepare a bowl and add 500 ml water and 2 tsp salt. Mix well and then add the clams. Leave to soak for 1 hour to purge them of sand.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Drain the water and rinse the clams once more to remove any leftover sand or debris. Transfer to a large pot and add 3 tbsp sake.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Heat on medium and once the sake starts to bubble, reduce the heat to simmer and cover with a lid. Steam with the lid on for 5 minutes or until all of the clams have opened.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Remove the lid and add ½ tbsp butter and 1 tsp Japanese light soy sauce (usukuchi shoyu). Gently shake the pan to mix the butter and soy sauce until melted.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Serve up, drizzle with the sauce leftover in the pan and sprinkle with finely chopped green onions. Enjoy!

title: Creamy Red Bean Popsicles あずきバー
description: These red bean ice cream, called Azuki Bars, are a creamy and delicious treat that are perfect for hot summer days and to eat as a yummy Japanese dessert!

ingredients.name: sweet red bean paste (Azuki bean paste (Store bought or home made Azuki bean paste)*1)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Bring the milk and cream to a simmer over low heat in a sauce pan.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Turn the heat off and set aside.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Whisk 2 egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until the colour of the mixture becomes pale and fluffy.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Add the sweet red bean paste to the sugar and yolk mixture and mix well.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Gradually pour the warm milk mixture into the egg mixture and keep whisking until smooth.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Pour the mixture into a clean sauce pan and place over low heat for 5 minutes, continuously stirring.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Leave it in the fridge to chill.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Pour the chilled mixture into an ice cream maker (or you can pour the mixture straight into the mould if you don't mind the segments precipitating at the bottom).

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Run the ice cream maker for about 20 minutes, and once the mixture has become thicker, pour it into a popsicle mould and freeze it overnight or 7-8 hours.

title: Kelp-Cured Sea Bream Sashimi (Tai no Kombu-Jime)
description: Enjoy the enhanced flavor and unique texture of sea bream sashimi cured with kombu using a traditional technique called "kombu-jime". This recipe also includes how to make a simple dashi soy sauce for dipping!

ingredients.name: sheets dried kelp (kombu) (large enough to cover the surface of the sea bream)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Place 2 fillets sashimi-grade sea bream in a wide container and evenly sprinkle both sides with ¼ tsp salt.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Cover the container and place it in the refrigerator with one side propped up. This will allow any liquid that comes out to trickle to the bottom of the container. Rest for 1 hour.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Gently rub the surface of 2 sheets dried kelp (kombu) with a lightly dampened cloth to remove any dust or debris, then place them in a container and rub with ½ tbsp sake. Rest for 1 hour to soften.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: After an hour, drain any accumulated liquid and pat the surface of the fish dry with kitchen paper.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Pat each sheet of kombu dry with kitchen paper and then sandwich the sea bream fillets between them.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Wrap with plastic wrap and rest in the refrigerator for 1 day.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Mix 1 ½ tbsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) and 1 ½ tbsp dashi stock together and pour into individual dipping bowls.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Unwrap the sea bream and cut into thin slices. Discard the kombu or use it for decoration when plating up.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Serve alongside the dipping sauce and wasabi paste. Enjoy!

title: Strawberry Daifuku 苺大福
description: Japanese people favourite Strawberry Daifuku recipe.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: wash the strawberries and cut off stems.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Divide the white bean paste into 30g balls.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Flatten the white bean paste and place a strawberry (pointy end down) on the center.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: wrap the strawberry with white bean paste and shape it back into a round ball. Set aside

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Place Shiratamako and sugar in a large heat proof bowl and add water.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Stir and mix well

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Cover with cling wrap and microwave for 1 minute and 30 seconds to 2 minutes depending on the microwave. It should look partly floury and partly should be starting to resemble mocha texture.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Take the bowl out of the microwave, stir well with a wooden spatula and microwave further for 1 minute. The mochi should look translucent.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Scatter enough Karakuriko (potato starch) on the rolling mat and empty the mochi from the bowl onto the starch

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Divide the mochi into 6 pieces and roll out flat till each circle is around 10 cm in diameter.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Place the white bean paste wrapped strawberry (strawberry tip facing down) on the rolled out mochi.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Gather the edge of mochi wrapping and wrap the strawberry with mochi using well dusted hands.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Close the mochi ends at the top with your well dusted finger and shape it into a nice round shaped daifuku mochi.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Repeat the above process for the remaining mochi and strawberries.

title: Homemade Koshian (Smooth Sweet Red Bean Paste)
description: Learn how to make Koshian, a smooth and sweet bean paste (anko) made from red adzuki beans. This popular filling is essential for many Japanese desserts.

ingredients.name: sugar (I use 60% white sugar, 40% light brown sugar)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Pour 200 g dry adzuki beans into a bowl and fill it with water until the beans are fully covered. Swill the beans around and then drain the water. Repeat 2-3 times to wash.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Transfer the beans to a pot and fill with fresh water until they are submerged. The water should cover the beans by 1-2 inches. Bring to a boil over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Drain the water and discard.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Rinse out the pot and pour the beans back in. Fill the pot with fresh water once more, making sure the beans are fully submerged. Again, the water should be 1-2 inches higher than the beans.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Bring to a boil over a medium heat once more and scoop out any foam that forms on the surface of the water.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Once it's boiling, lower the heat slightly and place a drop lid on top. Gently boil until the beans are fully softened (usually about 40 mins to 1 hour). Check the beans occasionally, stir them and top up the water as necessary so that they're always submerged.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: After 40 minutes, take a few of the larger beans, run them under cold water to cool them down, and smudge them between your thumb and forefinger. If they're soft enough to spread like a paste, the beans are fully cooked. If it's a little hard or grainy, continue to cook. Check every 5-10 minutes until they're soft to the core.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Once soft, turn off the heat. Place a fine-mesh sieve over a heatproof bowl and pour the beans through.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Crush the beans thoroughly, pushing them through the sieve as you go. I used a pestle to grind them. Pour water over them occasionally to make loosen the insides of the beans from the skins.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Scrape the bottom of the sieve into the bowl to catch all of the bean paste, then fill the bowl with fresh water. Note: For an even smoother result, you can pour the mixture into a food processor and blitz before pouring it back into the bowl.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until the paste has sunk to the bottom. Carefully pour out the top water, being careful not to pour away any of the bean paste, and refill with fresh water. Repeat 3 times in total (this step improves the flavor of the bean paste).

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Pour the bean paste into a cheesecloth and squeeze out all of the water. Set aside for now.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Add 175 g sugar to a saucepan along with 2-3 tbsp of water. Heat on medium-low and stir continuously until the sugar has dissolved.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Mix the red bean paste into the melted sugar and mix continuously over the heat until you can draw a line across the bottom of the pan. (Be careful not to overcook as it will firm up once cooled).

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Turn off the heat and mix in ¼ tsp salt.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.description: Transfer to a wide container and cover with plastic wrap touching the surface to stop it from drying out. Leave to cool to room temperature, then eal the container with a lid and store in the fridge for up to 3 days. Alternatively, divide into portions and freeze for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Step 17
steps.description: Use your homemade koshian red bean paste to make a variety of Japanese desserts!

title: Tekka Don Recipe
description: Tuna Sashimi over steamed rice with savory soy sauce

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: In a small pot, combine the soy sauce, Sake, and Mirin and bring to a boil. Remove from heat immediately, and let cool.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Cut the tuna sashimi into 1/2"(1cm) thick pieces.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Marinade Tuna pieces in cooled soy sauce mixture (or Mentsuyu) for 10-15 minutes.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Serve rice in a bowl, and top with marinated tuna, sesame seeds, wasabi, and Roasted Seaweed. Pour some of the marinade sauce over rice if you want.

title: Shiozake Japanese salted salmon 塩鮭
description: Shiozake is Japanese salted salmon. It is usually served as main dish for breakfast with other side dishes such as egg rolls. Also it is popular for Obento.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Pat dry the salmon fillets with kitchen paper towel.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Pour and sprinkle sake over salmon fillets.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Sprinkle salt on both sides of salmon fillets.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Wrap the salmon fillets with kitchen paper towel and cling wrap over.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Refrigerate the fillets over night or at least 7-8 hours.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Grill for 7-8 minutes in the oven at 180 degrees celsius.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Serve with plain steamed rice.

title: Rose dumplings 餃子ローズ
description: Hot to make beautiful Rose dumplings with step by step photos and a video

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Chop the cabbage and green shallots finely. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt over it and leave it for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Squeeze out the excess water from the cabbage and shallots. Place them in a mixing bowl. *3

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add the pork mince and all sauces to the bowl and mix them together till the mince becomes a bit sticky.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Place one wrapper on a chopping board and wet one side edge with water and overwrap with another wrapper.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Repeat the same with two more wrappers (altogether 4).

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Spoon about a heaped teaspoon amount of the pork mixture onto the centre of each gyoza wrapper.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Wet the edge of the wrappers with water with your finger and fold them in half from the right-hand side.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Seal and close up the gyoza wrapper firmly and roll them up from one side.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Wet the end of one side of the gyoza rose to close the gyoza. Repeat this step with 28 wrappers to make 8 gyoza roses altogether.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Heat some oil in a frying pan over medium heat and place the gyoza in the pan and let the bottom of the rose brown.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Pour 1/4 cup of water into the pan and put a lid on it to steam the gyoza for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Take the lid off and let the water evaporate. Turn off the heat and serve the gyoza on a plate.

title: Deep-Fried Oyster (Kaki Fry)
description: Deep-fried Panko coated oyster

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Make salt water (mix 1 litter or 4 cups of water plus 1 tsp salt, not in the ingredients above). Wash oysters in salt water. Drain cloudy water and pat dry well with paper towels. Salt and pepper lightly.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Coat the oysters lightly with flour, dip in egg, then cover with bread crumbs. Handle gently so that the oysters don't get squashed.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Heat deep frying oil to 350 F, and deep fry the crumb-covered oysters. You can check the temperature by dropping a bread crumb in the oil. If it comes up to the oil surface right after it's dropped in, the oil is ready.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Fry until the color turns golden brown and the oysters float in the oil, about 3 minutes, turning a couple times as they cook.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Serve with Tonkatsu Sauce and lemon if you want.

title: Lemon Teriyaki Pork Chops
description: These succulent pork chops are pan-fried with an addictive teriyaki-style glaze flavored with zesty lemon slices. Ready in 20 minutes and perfect for lunch or dinner!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Place 2 boneless pork chop on a chopping board and make cuts through the thick fatty parts. This will prevent curling and improve the texture.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Sprinkle with 1 pinch salt on each side and set aside.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Cut 1 clove garlic into thin slices. Heat a pan on medium-low and add 1 tbsp cooking oil. Add the garlic slices and fry until crispy on both sides.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Transfer the garlic chips to kitchen paper to absorb the excess oil.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Using the same pan, increase the heat to medium-high and add the seasoned pork chops. Fry for 1½-2 minutes on one side or until golden.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Flip them over, lower the heat to low-medium and cover with a lid. Continue to fry for 3-4 minutes.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: While you wait, cut 1 king oyster mushroom (eryngii) into bitesize pieces. Mix 2 tbsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu), 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake and ½ tbsp honey in a small bowl to make the teriyaki sauce.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Once the time is up, add the king oyster mushrooms and teriyaki sauce.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Sauté until the mushrooms have softened and the teriyaki sauce has thickened slightly. Flip the pork chops to coat them evenly on both sides.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Add 4 slices lemon to the pan and increase the heat. Continue to cook until the sauce is thickened to a syrup-like consistency.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Once it's thickened to your liking, remove the pan from the heat and transfer the pork to serving plates. Rest for 3 minutes before serving and garnish with lemon slices, leftover sauce from the pan and the sautéed mushrooms.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Yudofu Recipe
description: Tofu in Kombu broth with Ponzu dipping sauce

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Put water and Kombu together in a pot and let boil, then turn down heat to medium low.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Cut Tofu into 8 blocks and add to the pot. Cover and simmer for 7-8 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Serve with Ponzu, green onions, and Shichimi.

title: Beef Negimaki 牛肉のネギ巻き
description: Beef negimaki is a Japanese home-cooking staple which is easy, quick and delicious to make. Perfect for weekday dinner & bento boxes!

ingredients.name: tbs plain flour or potato starch(Katakuriko)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cut the blanched scallions into 5cm (2 inch) wide strips. Cut carrots into sticks and cut green beans in half then parboil them and set aside.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Lay the thinly slice beef on a chopping board and place prepared scallions and vegetables on the beef then tightly roll it up. The beef strip should be about 20cm (8 inch) long. If the meat is shorter than that, overwrap beef slices slightly to make it 20cm (8 inch) long.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: You can secure by using a toothpick to tie the end of the meat (optional)

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Repeat this same process until all the beef is used (I made about 8 negimaki out of 300 g beef)

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Cover the roll ups with flour.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Heat a little sesame oil in a frying pan over medium heat and place the beef roll ups in the pan.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Cook one side for about 2- 3 minutes or until browned with a lid on.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Turn the beef roll ups over and cook the other side for a further 2-3 minutes.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Combine all the sauce ingredients and pour over the beef roll ups in the frying pan to sizzle.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Serve with green salad and rice.

title: Japanese Seasoned Salmon Flakes
description: These succulent salmon flakes are delicately seasoned with Japanese condiments and are the perfect pairing for rice, especially rice balls!

ingredients.name: salmon fillets ((lean fillets), approximately 100g per fillet)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Pat the surface of 2 salmon fillets dry with kitchen paper. Rub ½ tsp salt on both sides and rest for 10 minutes. While you wait, start boiling a pot of water.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: After 10 minutes, the salt will have drawn out the excess moisture, so pat dry once more.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Once the water is boiling, turn the heat down to a simmer and add the salmon. Simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Take the salmon out of the pan and gently shake off the excess water. Transfer it to a container and carefully pull off the skin (you can fry this and eat it as a snack, or discard). Use a spatula to break it up and remove any bones with tweezers.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Heat a frying pan on low to medium-low and add 1 tsp butter. Once melted, add the salmon flakes along with ½ tbsp sake, ½ tbsp mirin and ⅛ tsp salt. Mix well and continue to heat until the liquid has almost gone.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Turn off the heat, and mix in ¼ tsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) and 1 tsp toasted white sesame seeds.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Use straight away or transfer to a clean container and leave to cool. Once cool to the touch, cover and store in the fridge for up to 5 days.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Enjoy with rice!

title: Japanese Rice Porridge with Sweet potato いも茶がゆ
description: Japanese rice porridge, or 'okayu', is a warm and delicious comfort food. It's so soft and easy to digest so it's a perfect dish for when you're sick!

ingredients.name: Japanese tea bag of any kind

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cut the sweet potato into bite size pieces and leave them in a bowl of water.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Wash and rinse the uncooked rice until the washing water becomes clear then drain with a strainer.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Place the drained rice and 10 cups of water in a large pan.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Bring it to boil over high heat then add a tea bag.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Turn the heat down to medium to simmer to cook the rice for about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Drain the water from the sweet potatoes and add into the pan.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Simmer for a further 10 min to cook the sweet potato bits.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Serve in a rice bowl.

title: Yakiudon (Stir-Fried Udon)
description: Stir-fried Udon with pork and vegetables simply seasoned with soy sauce

ingredients.name: servings of Udon noodles (2 frozen packets)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Defrost Udon noodles under running water. Strain water very well. Or prepare dried Udon noodles according to the directions on a package. Cut pork and vegetables into bite size pieces.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: In a frying pan, heat oil well at medium high heat. Add pork, and cook until brown. Add carrot, green pepper, and onion and stir fry for a minute. Add cabbage and cook further until vegetables get lightly wilted. Add Udon into the same pan and cook for a couple of minutes. Season with soy sauce and white pepper if you have it. Top with Katsuobushi and Benishoga if you like.

title: Onsen Tamago (Japanese Hot Spring Eggs)
description: Onsen Tamago is a boiled egg like no other! This unique cooking style produces beautifully set whites and silky semi-set yolks served in a light dashi-based sauce, perfect as part of a Japanese-inspired breakfast.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Measure out 300 ml cold water and place it in the refrigerator. It should be fully chilled before you start (about 10°C/50°F). Once chilled, add 1500 ml water to a pot and bring to a rolling boil. (Tip: Heating with a lid will speed up the process.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Once the water is thoroughly boiling, turn off heat and add the cold water from the fridge.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Immediately add 4 eggs straight from the fridge. At this point the water should be about 80 °C (176 °F).

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Place a lid on top and set a timer for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Remove the eggs and rest in a bowl at room temperature for exactly 3 minutes (5 minutes in winter). Use a timer to ensure accuracy. While you wait, prepare a bowl of ice cold water.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Once rested at room temperature, pour ice-cold water into the bowl to halt the cooking process and stop them from cooking any further. Rest for 5-10 minutes, this will help them come out cleanly before serving.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Combine 2 tbsp dashi stock, ½ tbsp Japanese light soy sauce (usukuchi shoyu), 1 tbsp mirin and 1 tbsp water in a small microwavable bowl. Microwave uncovered for 1 minute at 600W. The sauce can be served warm or cooled depending on preference

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Crack the egg into a serving bowl and add about 1 tbsp of sauce for each serving. Enjoy!

title: Teriyaki Tofu Donburi
description: This delicious tofu donburi is made with crispy cubes of firm tofu coated in a sticky teriyaki glaze and served with pan-fried green onions and bell peppers over a bed of fluffy rice.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Wrap 350 g firm tofu with kitchen paper and place it on a heatproof plate. Microwave for 2 minutes at 600W, then remove and leave to cool.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Heat a pan on medium and add a drizzle of cooking oil. Fry 50 g green bell pepper and 50 g Japanese leek (naganegi) until lightly charred, then transfer to a plate and set by the stove for later.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Once the tofu is cool to the touch, cut it into cubes. Larger cubes will make cooking easier later.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Take a small bowl and add a generous pinch of salt and pepper and 3 tbsp potato starch (katakuriko), mix well and sprinkle it on a plate or tray.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Reheat the same pan as earlier over medium and add a generous amount of cooking oil (approx 1 tbsp per serving). Once the pan is hot, coat the tofu pieces in the starch mixture and place them directly into the pan. Tip: Do not coat the tofu in advance as the starch will soak up the moisture and become sticky.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Fry the tofu and turn occasionally, ensuring they're golden brown on all sides.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Take a small bowl and mix 2 tbsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu), 2 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake, 2 tsp sugar and ½ tbsp garlic paste until well combined. Once the tofu is golden all over, pour the sauce into the pan.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Add the charred vegetables from earlier and continue to cook until warmed through and the glaze has become thick and glossy. Once everything is evenly coated, remove the pan from the heat.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Divide 2 portions cooked Japanese short-grain rice into serving bowls and place the tofu and vegetables on top. Sprinkle with toasted white sesame seeds, finely chopped green onions and a drizzle of chili oil (rayu).

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Matcha Black Sesame Cookies 抹茶黒胡麻クッキー
description: updated recipe for easy and delicious Matcha black sesame seeds cookies

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Sift the flour and matcha together and add almond meal. Set aside.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Place the butter and caster sugar in a bowl and mix well until the colour of the butter becomes whitish and creamy (I used a stand mixer with the whisk attachment).

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Add the egg to the bowl and beat well.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Change the attachment to a blade attachment and add sifted flour and almond meal to the bowl. *2

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Add black sesame seeds as well and combine them all together but try not to over mix.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Separate the dough into two and form into two balls.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Wrap the cookie dough in plastic wrap and roll it into a long round 4 cm in diameter or square shape then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. *3

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Preheat the oven to 180 degree Celsius.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Cut the cookie dough into 5mm thick slices then place on a baking tray lined with baking paper.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Bake for 25 minutes then remove from oven and allow to cool on a wire rack. *4

title: Barazushi
description: Mixed sushi with cooked vegetables topped with thinly sliced egg crepes

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cut carrot thinly. Hydrate dried Shiitake mushrooms for 15 minutes, squeeze out water, and cut thinly. Cut Takenoko into small pieces.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: In a pot, let boil Dashi, soy sauce, Mirin, and sugar, add all the vegetables (except snow peas), and cook at medium heat for 5-7 minutes until the liquid is almost evaporated. Let it cool.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: In a large deep dish, mix Sushi Rice and cooked vegetables well.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Serve on an individual plate with Kinshitamago, Roasted Seaweed, sliced snow peas, and Benishoga on top.

title: Marinated Yellowtail Sashimi (Buri no Ryukyu)
description: How to make regional Buri no Ryukyu with fresh yellowtail sashimi marinated in a delicious soy-based sauce.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Cut 200 g sashimi-grade yellowtail into thin slices using your preferred method.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Hirazukuri Method (Recommended for Dorsal Meat)

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Sogigiri Method (Recommended for Belly)

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Buri no Ryukyu Marinade

title: An Pan (Bread Roll with Sweet Red Bean)
description: Fluffy bread rolls stuffed with Anko sweet red bean paste

ingredients.name: egg wash: 1 egg plus pinch of salt (mixed well)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Put lukewarm milk, yeast, and sugar in a stand mixer bowl, then whisk well. Let it sit for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Combine bread flour and cake flour, and add to the milk mixture. Add salt and milk powder, and start the mixer kneading with a dough hook at medium speed.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: When the dough is becoming a ball (after about 8 minutes), add soft butter and knead for another 4-5 minutes until the butter is completely incorporated. Cover with plastic, and leave in a warm place about 1 hour until the dough has doubled in size.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Make balls of Anko, each 1.5" (or 4cm) in diameter and about 1 1/4oz (or 35g).

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Take the dough and deflate the gas from the dough. Put on to a cutting board, and cut into 8 equal pieces about 2.5oz (or 70g) each. Form into small balls. Let them rest for 15 minutes covered.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Flatten a ball of dough with a rolling pin to a 4" (or 10cm) round. Put a ball of Anko in the center of the round, wrap with dough, and pinch the ends of the dough so that the Anko is sealed inside the dough ball. Repeat for remaining dough and Anko.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Place shaped dough balls on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper leaving 2" (or 5cm) space between the balls. Brush egg wash (the mixture of egg with a pinch of salt) on the surface of the dough, and sprinkle some black sesame seeds on top. Leave them to double in size, about 1 hour.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Bake in a preheated oven at 400F(205C) for about 10 minutes until they brown.

title: Homemade Japanese Curry Roux
description: Ditch the pre-made curry cubes and try making your Japanese-style roux from home! This curry roux paste is rich in flavor and can be made ahead of time, perfect for meal prep!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Add 3 ½ tsp Japanese style curry powder and 2 ½ tsp ground cumin to a dry pan and heat on medium. Mix them over the heat them until the flavor is released and the color has darkened slightly.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Take a new pan and heat on medium. Once hot, add 1 tbsp beef suet (fat) and spread it around the pan as it melts. Add 3 cloves garlic and 15 g ginger root to the pan, and fry until fragrant.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Next, add 200 g onion and fry until golden and translucent.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Reduce the heat to medium-low and continue to fry the onions until dark brown, soft and caramelized. This will take approximately 30 minutes. Stir occasionally and add 50 ml water halfway through to stop it sticking to the bottom of the pan.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Once the liquid has reduced to nothing and the onions resemble a thick paste, remove the beef fat and add 3 tbsp all-purpose flour. Mix until combined.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Next, add the toasted curry powder and cumin from earlier, and mix until evenly distributed through the roux.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Measure out 900 ml beef bouillon and add a small amount to the pan. Break up the roux and whisk until smooth and thick.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Add the rest of the bouillon gradually, whisking thoroughly each time to prevent lumps.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Add 2 tsp coriander powder, 3 tbsp orange marmalade, ½ tsp ground cloves, 1 tsp cardamom powder and 2 tsp ginger powder to the mixture and whisk until incorporated.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Add 1 bay leaf and simmer for 2 hours, stirring occasionally and removing any foam from the top using a mesh spoon.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Once it has thickened to a paste consistency, transfer the roux to a container and leave to cool.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Once cool, cover and store in the fridge for up to 1 week. To freeze, divide it into portions and freeze for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: To use, seal your meat in a large pot, then add your vegetables, homemade curry roux and approx 600-700ml of water. Mix well and simmer until thickened. It takes about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Japanese Baked Cheesecake ベイクドチーズケーキ
description: This Japanese Baked Cheesecake is super simple to make and is so deliciously rich and creamy, you'll be fighting with everyone over the last slice!

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Preheat your oven to 356°F (180°C)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Leave the Philadelphia cheese and eggs out until they become room temperature.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: In a bowl, break the digestive biscuits (Graham Crackers) to crumbs and combine with melted butter.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Line the bottom of the baking form with parchment paper and spread butter thinly on the side of the baking tin. *4

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Evenly pour the biscuit crumb and butter mixture into the bottom of the tin to create the crust then set it aside.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Firstly, beat the Philadelphia cheese in a mixing bowl. While continuously beating the mixture, add the sugar, then the eggs, then the cream, then finally the lemon juice. Mix it all together for a few minutes once all the ingredients have been added until it becomes creamy and plump.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Add the sifted flour (even though it's only 3 tbsp) to the mixture and fold it lightly.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Pour the mixture into the prepared tins and place in preheated oven.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Turn the heat down to 338°F(170°C) and bake for about 60 minutes depending on your oven.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Turn the heat down to 320°F(160°C) and bake another 20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: The top of the cake should be golden brown. Turn the heat off take it out of the oven.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Allow the cheesecakes to cool down in the baking tin then cover them with cling wrap and leave them in the fridge overnight or for a few hours. *5

steps.title: Step 13

title: Sweet Potato Tempura (3 Japanese Ways to Make)
description: Sweet potatoes' melt-in-mouth texture and natural sweetness make them one of the best vegetables to use for tempura.

ingredients.name: unbleached cake flour (or all purpose + extra for dusting)
Japanese mayonnaise (or half a small whisked egg)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Measure out 75 ml cold water into a jug and place it in the fridge for 20-30 minutes. Place the sparkling water in the fridge too. (Preferably an unopened bottle, measure after chilling.)

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Sift 15 g cornstarch and 75 g unbleached cake flour into a bowl. Mix them together and place the bowl in the fridge for 20-30 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: While your tempura batter ingredients are chilling, wash the surface of 600 g Japanese sweet potato (satsumaimo), cut off the ends, and slice according to your preferred method from the post above. (Thin rounds, thick rounds or sticks/wedges.) Make sure every piece has some skin left on. (If using thick rounds, cut a shallow cross pattern on the front and back of each piece.)

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Soak the cut pieces in cold water for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Once your batter ingredients have been chilling in the fridge for 30 minutes, start preheating your cooking oil to 160 °C (320 °F).

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: In a bowl (or jug), add a few tbsp of the chilled water and ½ tbsp Japanese mayonnaise. Whisk until well combined to loosen up the mayo, then pour the rest of the chilled water and 50 ml carbonated water (chilled) into the bowl.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Add the flour/starch mixture to the water one-third at a time, gently drawing crosses through the mixture with the chopsticks to incorporate it. Do not whisk or over-mix, it's fine for the batter to have lumps.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Optional step: Add 2 ice cubes to the batter and mix to make it extra cold.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Test your oil by adding a drop of batter; if it sizzles and floats, you're ready to fry.Dry the sweet potato pieces with kitchen paper and coat them with a thin layer of flour. Dip them in the batter and then immediately place them into the oil. Make sure not to overfill the pot. (Keep the batter in the fridge or freezer between batches.) For thin rounds or sticks, fry for 4-5 minutes, turning over halfway through. For thick slices, fry for 6-7 minutes or until you can easily pierce the center with a skewer.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Once cooked, place on a wire rack to allow the excess oil to drip off.

steps.title: Step 11

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Measure out 75 ml water into a jug and place it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes along with an unopened bottle of sparkling water.

steps.title: Step 5

steps.title: Step 7

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: In a bowl (or jug), add a few tbsp of the chilled water and ½ tbsp Japanese mayonnaise. Mix until combined, then add the rest of the chilled water and 50 ml carbonated water into the bowl.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Add the flour/starch one-third at a time, gently drawing crosses through the mixture with the chopsticks to incorporate it. (Do not whisk or over-mix.)

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Add a couple of ice cubes to the batter and mix to make it extra cold. (optional)

steps.title: Step 11

title: Taiyaki (Japanese Fish Shaped Waffle)
description: Taiyaki is a golden waffle-like snack filled with sweet red bean paste and shaped like a fish. It's crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside and a well-loved Japanese street food snack.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Sift the dry ingredients (25 g cornstarch, 125 g unbleached cake flour, ½ tsp baking soda and ½ tsp baking powder) into a bowl and mix.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: In a separate bowl add 20 g light brown sugar and 1 egg. Whisk until combined, then add ½ tbsp honey, 1 pinch salt, 1 drop vanilla essence, 1 tsp cooking oil and mix well. Finally, pour in 150 ml whole milk while whisking until smooth.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Make a well in the dry ingredients and add the liquid ingredients one-third at a time, whisking gently each time until the ingredients are combined and smooth.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Cover the bowl and rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Divide 240 g red bean paste (anko) into equal pieces for each taiyaki, approx 40g (2.5oz) each. Roll into cylinders, cover and store in the refrigerator until it's time to cook.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: After 30 minutes have passed, grease both sides of the taiyaki pan with a thin layer of cooking oil. Use kitchen paper to spread it evenly into the grooves of the mold. Place one side of the mold onto the stove and turn the heat on low/medium-low. Heat for a few minutes.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Once hot, add 1 tbsp of batter to each heated mold and spread it around using the back of a spoon. Make sure to go over edges of the taiyaki shape to stop it from falling when you flip the mold.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Once it's set (cooked enough that it doesn't run out), flip so that the empty one is on the stove and add 1 tbsp of batter to each mold. Spread evenly with the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Place an anko cylinder into the centre of each taiyaki.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Drizzle another tbsp of the batter over the top of the anko filling to act as a glue.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Close the mold and heat for another 1 1/2 to 2 minutes on each side. (This varies from stove to stove so make sure not to leave it unattended, you can flip it when you can smell the sweet, baked smell of taiyaki.)

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Remove the cooked taiyaki from the mold and repeat until you've used all of the batter and anko.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Optional: Use kitchen scissors to trim around the edges to neaten up the shape.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Edamame Soybeans Potage 枝豆のポタージュ

title: Spinach Ohitashi (Japanese Spinach Salad in Dashi)
description: Spinach Ohitashi is a vegetable dish made with blanched spinach soaked in a savory dashi-based marinade. It's simple and makes a great side dish for any Japanese meal!

ingredients.name: salt (1% the weight of cooking water)
bonito flakes (katsuobushi) (optional garnish, replace with sesame seeds for plant-based diets)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Wash 200 g Oriental spinach, paying careful attention to the roots where sometimes dirt and sand can become lodged.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Place the spinach in a bowl of cold water and rest for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Take a small saucepan and add 240 ml dashi stock, 2 tbsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) and 2 tbsp mirin. Bring to a boil and let it bubble for 2 minutes before removing the pan from the heat. This base sauce is called "hitashi-ji" or "happo-ji".

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Heat 2 liters water in a separate pot and prepare a bowl of ice-cold water. Once the pot of water is boiling, add 1 tbsp salt (approx 1% weight of the water) and mix to dissolve. Drain the spinach and place it in the pot so that the stems are submerged but the leaves are poking out. Boil for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: After 30 seconds, use tongs or chopsticks to press down the rest of the spinach, submerging the leaves. Blanch for 15 seconds.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Immediately transfer the blanched spinach to the bowl of ice water and leave to chill for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Remove the spinach from the bowl after 10 minutes and gently squeeze out the water. Place them on a bamboo sushi mat and roll it tightly.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Squeeze the sushi mat firmly over a sink to remove as much water as possible.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Unroll the mat and place it on a flat surface with the spinach still in place. Pour 1 tbsp of the hitashi-ji over the spinach to remove any remaining water.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Wrap the spinach with the sushi mat again and squeeze once more.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Transfer the spinach to a lidded container and pour the remaining hitashi-ji over the top. If the spinach is not fully submerged, press plastic wrap directly over the surface. Cover with a lid and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, overnight if time permits.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: Cut off the stems and cut into bitesize pieces.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Divide into serving bowls with a drizzle of hitashi-ji and a sprinkle of bonito flakes (katsuobushi). Serve as a side dish with Japanese-style meals and enjoy!

title: Dango Recipe

title: Matcha Green Tea Ice Cream
description: This luxurious and creamy homemade ice cream combined with the subtly bitter and earthy flavor of Japanese green tea makes the perfect dessert or snack any time of year. You can make this recipe by hand or in an ice cream machine!

ingredients.name: heavy cream (35% milk fat or higher)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: Pour 200 ml whole milk and 200 ml heavy cream into a saucepan and heat on medium while stirring. Once bubbles start to form around the edges (or it reaches 60 °C (140 °F)-70 °C (158 °F)) remove it from the heat.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Add 2 pasteurized egg yolk, 75 g sugar and 1 tsp cornstarch to a heatproof bowl and whisk until pale and smooth.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: Temper the egg mixture by adding 1 ladle of hot milk/cream to the bowl while whisking.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Continue to whisk and gradually add the rest of the hot milk/cream.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Wipe the residue off the pan and then pour the mixture back in through a sieve.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Sift in 1 ½ tbsp matcha powder and then turn on the heat to low/medium low.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Whisk thoroughly until the matcha is incorporated.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Stir continuously using a silicone spatula and scrape the bottom to prevent burning. Once the mixture reaches a thick, custard-like consistency, remove from the heat.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Transfer it to a steel bowl placed in an ice bath. Stir for a few minutes to release some of the heat, then cover the surface with plastic wrap to prevent a skin forming on the top. Leave to cool for 10-20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Once cool to the touch, transfer to a wide container with a lid and place in the freezer for 30 minutes. (Tip: It will freeze faster in a wide container rather than a tall one.)

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: After 30 minutes, take it out from the freezer and whisk for 1 minute. Return to the freezer and churn every 30-45 minutes for 3-4 hours. (Set a timer so you don't forget!)

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: If the mixture becomes too hard to whisk, switch to a spatula and make sure to scrape down the sides and mix them into the center.Once you've finished churning, freeze for about 2-3 hours. (It can take longer depending on the weather, the temperature of your freezer, and size of your container.)

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Remove from the freezer for 5-10 minutes before serving. (This will soften it slightly and make it easier to scoop.)

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: Enjoy!

title: Sakana no Nitsuke (Japanese simmered fish)
description: Sakana no nitsuke is a delicious fish dish simmered in a flavourful sauce consisting of classic Japanese condiments such as soy sauce, sake, mirin and ginger.

ingredients.name: white fish fillets (flatfish, flounder, snapper or similar)
Japanese mustard spinach (komatsuna) ((komatsuna) or regular spinach/bok choi)

steps.title: Step 1
steps.description: First, sprinkle 200 g white fish fillets with a 2 pinches salt on each side and rest for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.description: Cut the 20 g ginger root into 2mm thick slices.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.description: After 10 minutes, use a sharp knife to make shallow incisions on the skin. This can be a cross or 2-3 diagonal lines. (If you're using a whole fish such as snapper, make incisions on both sides.)

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Prepare 1 of 1 bowl freshly boiled water and 1 1 bowl ice cold water.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.description: Swill the fish in the boiling water for 5 seconds, then transfer to the ice water.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.description: Remove it and dry with a paper towel.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.description: Pour 150 ml water, 150 ml sake, 3 tbsp mirin and 2 ½ tbsp sugar into a pan.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.description: Place over a medium heat and stir. Once the sugar is dissolved, add the ginger slices and fish with the skin side facing up.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.description: Once the broth starts to bubble, lower the heat and place a drop lid (instructions in post) on top of the fish. Simmer for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.description: Measure out 3 tbsp Japanese soy sauce (koikuchi shoyu) and remove the drop lid. Pour ⅓ of the soy sauce over the fish, and spoon the liquid in the pan over the fish. Once it is incorporated into the rest of the sauce, repeat until you've used all of the soy sauce.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.description: Return the drop lid to it's original position and simmer for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.description: While it's simmering, bring a small pot of water to the boil and cut 50 g Japanese mustard spinach (komatsuna) into 5cm (2 inch) pieces.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.description: Blanch for 1 minute, then remove from the heat and transfer to a bowl of cold water.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.description: After the fish has been simmering for 10 minutes, remove the drop lid and continue to spoon the sauce over the surface until the liquid is reduced to one-third of its original volume.

steps.title: Step 15
steps.description: Serve the fish fillets up on a plate, top with ginger and pour a few tablespoons of leftover sauce over the top. Squeeze the excess water out of the Japanese mustard spinach and place on the side of the plate.

steps.title: Step 16
steps.description: Enjoy!

description: This teriyaki cod is made with tender bitesize pieces of fried cod coated in a syrupy homemade teriyaki glaze. It is addictively delicious and easy to make too!

steps.title: Step 2

steps.title: Step 3

steps.title: Step 4
steps.description: Remove from the oil and transfer to a wire rack to let the excess oil drain off.

steps.title: Step 5

steps.title: Step 6
